build: PAL original, two-sided G64; level 1 load in play

comments.text: Entry of the level 1 file, jumped to by the resident loader at $0424. Sets up the title screen ($0A60), then loops between the high-score page ($11BC) and the credits page ($13C9), with pauses through $2027, until $0EEC sees fire and starts play.
A lone RTS, called first by the entry at $0A20.

Extended-colour flag: when it is not zero set_ecm ($1656) and set_ecm_bit ($163F) turn extended colour mode on, otherwise off, and the title interrupt at $1557 keeps the sprites off. Set to 1 by title_setup ($0A67, $0AF4), title_wait_fire ($0F2C), type_briefing ($0FD8), type_lab_text ($5866) and mask_setup ($58CD); cleared by title_setup at $0B3C, play_setup at $1B4E and mask_setup at $5A23.

Blanks the screen for a moment ($D011 bit 4 cleared, set again at $0A92) and switches the video chip to bank 3 ($DD00 bits 0-1 cleared), screen at $CC00 and characters at $E000 ($D018=$38), with extended colour mode on ($D011 bit 6), and banks out the ROMs ($01=$35).
One byte that title_setup ($0AE3) clears and title_idle ($1311) sets to 1 once the typed name has been put in the high-score table. No code in the level 1 file or the resident code reads it.

Exchanges 256 bytes of $0BD7 with $C000 and 256 bytes of $0CD7 with $C100 (it reads both and writes each to the other), so calling it twice puts everything back. Called by title_setup at $0AB5 and by title_wait_fire at $0F32.
Copies four rows of 21 bytes from $0B83, $0B98, $0BAD and $0BC2 to $CC09, $CC31, $CC59 and $CC81 in the screen matrix (rows 0 to 3, from column 9). Called once by title_setup at $0ABB.
Four rows of 21 screen codes ($0B83, $0B98, $0BAD, $0BC2) that draw_title_rows ($0B63) copies to rows 0 to 3 of the title screen.
Row 1 of the title logo, 21 screen codes, copied by draw_title_rows ($0B63) to $CC31 (screen row 1, column 9).
Row 2 of the title logo, 21 screen codes, copied by draw_title_rows ($0B63) to $CC59 (screen row 2, column 9).
Row 3 of the title logo, 21 screen codes, copied by draw_title_rows ($0B63) to $CC81 (screen row 3, column 9).
512 bytes of character shapes that swap_title_chars ($0B41) exchanges with the character data: $0BD7-$0CD6 with $C000 and $0CD7-$0DD6 with $C100.
The second half of title_shapes: 256 bytes ($0CD7-$0DD6, characters $20 to $3F of the title screen's set) that swap_title_chars ($0B41) exchanges with $C100-$C1FF.

Stores A in colour RAM from $D8A0 to $DBE7 (840 bytes: four runs of $D2 bytes, rows 4 to 24). Called by the high-score page ($11BE, with A=$0D), the name entry in title_idle ($1273, A=7) and the credits page ($13D0, A=7).

Stores A in the screen matrix from $CCA0 to $CFE7 (840 bytes: four runs of $D2 bytes, rows 4 to 24), the same rows as fill_colour_rows. Called with A=$3D by the high-score page ($11C3), the name entry ($126E) and the credits page ($13CB).
The key code read every frame by $0E30.

Reads the keyboard with CIA 1 into A. It first reads ports A and B as inputs and returns $FF at once when any of bits 0-4 reads low (a joystick is held, the test at $0E3F); otherwise it scans the lines from $0EA7 and returns the key code from key_table, or $FF when no key is down, again giving $FF if a joystick bit reads low after the key is found ($0E8D). title_irq_bottom ($1623) and $1EF4 keep the result in $0E2F.

The value read_keys ($0E30) writes to CIA 1 port A ($DC00) to select one keyboard line: it starts at $FE and is rotated left through the carry after each line, so a single 0 bit walks along the eight lines.
The number of the keyboard line (0 to 7) read_keys ($0E30) is looking at; it starts at 0 and goes up by 1 after each line that holds no key. read_keys ORs it into the index of key_table ($0EAA).

The port B byte ($DC01) after read_keys ($0E30) has shifted it right to the bit that was clear. When key_table gives $FF for that key, read_keys reloads it at $0E9B and goes on looking at the remaining bits.

The key codes of the 64 keys of the keyboard matrix, 8 bytes for each bit of CIA 1 port B and in the order of the keyboard lines (port A bit 0 to 7). read_keys ($0E30) takes the entry at 8 times the bit number plus $0EA8. Letters and digits are ASCII, space is $20, RETURN is 0, DEL is 1, RUN/STOP is $7F and a key with no meaning is $FF.

Which attract page is up. title_wait_fire flips it and then shows the credits page for 0 and the high-score table for 1; the entry at $0A2C reads it the other way round, showing the high-score table for 0 and the credits for 1. title_setup sets it to 1 ($0AF1) and title_idle to 0 ($1269) after a name has been entered.

Title loop step: polls the joystick byte $203B for fire (bit 4 clear) and, every time the high byte $203A of the countdown $2039/$203A reaches 0, reloads it ($203A=2, $2039=$32) and flips $0EEA to swap between the credits and score pages. Fire starts the briefing ($0F44) and jumps to play_loop ($179E).

Set to 1 by title_wait_fire ($0F24) when fire starts the game and cleared by title_setup ($0AD7). While it is not zero the title interrupt at $1561 writes 0 to $D015, so no sprite shows during the briefing.
Countdown used by type_briefing ($0F44) and type_lab_text ($57E5): loaded with $1E, so that fire cannot stop the typing before $1E characters have been typed.
Index of the next character of the text being typed by type_briefing ($0F44) or type_lab_text ($57E5).

Types the level briefing text at $0FE6 onto the screen from $CC7E, one character at a time. A space code gives $3D and any other code gets $66 added; $FF ends a line (the pointer moves down $50 bytes, two screen rows) and a second $FF ends the text. It first fills the screen with $3D and colour RAM with 7, then waits $32 between characters; fire (bit 4 of $203B) stops the typing once the countdown $0F42 from $1E has run out, and at the end it waits for fire. It sets $0A5F to 1 and calls $A91A with A=4 before waiting for $A8EB to return zero. Called by title_wait_fire at $0F27.
Holds the Y register saved by type_briefing at $0F88: the immediate operand of the LDY at $0F90, so the offset into the screen row survives the delay.

The rest of type_briefing ($0F44). It takes the next code of the text at $0FE6 through the index $0F43. $FF ends a line: the index moves on, a second $FF in a row ends the text, otherwise the pointer $E1/$E2 moves down $50 bytes and Y goes back to 0. A space gives $3D and any other code gets $66 added before it is stored through ($E1),y and the typing goes on at $0F67. At the end it waits for fire ($203B bit 4 clear), sets $0A5F to 1, calls $A91A with A=4 and loops on $A8EB until it returns zero.

Screen-code text of the level 1 briefing, $0FE6 to $10A2, typed by type_briefing ($0F44) from $CC7E. Letters are codes 1 to 26, $20 is a space, $1B a full stop and $FF ends a line; a second $FF in a row ends the text. The lines, with the start of each: $0FE6 " LEVEL ONE.", $0FF2 a line of six spaces, $0FF9 " DARKMAN  SEEKING REVENGE ON", $1016 " THOSE WHO DISFIGURED HIM", $1033 " SETS OUT TO ACQUIRE THE ILL", $1050 " GOTTEN GAINS OF ROBERT G.", $106D " DURANT TO FURTHER HIS PLANS.", $108B six spaces and $1092 " END OF LINE...". The text goes on at $1000 (level_intro_text_part_2).

The rest of the briefing text of level_intro_text ($0FE6), from the middle of its line at $0FF9 to the closing $FF $FF at $10A1 and $10A2. A data symbol cannot reach across the memory-map edge at $1000, so the text has a second symbol here.
The high-score table: five records of 18 bytes, each a name of 10 codes followed by 8 score digits, the highest score first. insert_score ($114F) keeps it sorted.
The eight score digits of the fifth and last record of the high-score table (the record at $10EB), the score that high_score_check ($1110) compares the player's score with.

The record for the score just earned: the name from $1357 in its first 8 bytes and, from $1107, the score digits copied from $0A00 by high_score_check ($1110). insert_score ($114F) sorts it into the table.
The eight score digits of new_score: high_score_check ($1110) copies the player's score from $0A00-$0A07 here, and insert_score ($114F) moves the whole record into the table.

Set to 1 by high_score_check ($1110) when the score is higher than the last record of the table and to 0 otherwise; play_setup also clears it. Read by title_setup ($0AC3), which uses it to pick the tune, and by title_idle ($1261).

Sets $110F to 1 when the score, the eight digits $0A00-$0A07, is greater than the score of the last record of the high-score table (the digits at $10F5-$10FC), and to 0 otherwise. It copies the score to $1107-$110E first. Called by title_wait_fire at $0F3D and by title_idle at $125A.
Copies the eight name characters from name_buffer ($1357) to new_score ($10FD) and calls insert_score ($114F): the same steps as $1301-$130C in title_idle. Nothing calls or jumps to it.

Puts the new high score in the table. Copies the eight-character name from $1357 to $10FD, the first bytes of the new record at $10FD (its score digits are at $1107). Then, starting with the last record, it compares the score digits (offsets 10 to 17 of an 18-byte record) of the new record with the record above and, while the new one is higher, swaps the two records, up to five times. Called by title_idle at $130C and by the code at $114B.

The heading of the high-score page, "TODAYS TOP  DARKMEN" (two spaces before DARKMEN), in screen codes ($D7 is the space; show_scores adds $66, which makes it the blank character $3D). show_scores ($11BC) draws the first 19 bytes to $CD22; the twentieth, a space, is not drawn.

Draws the high-score page. Colours rows 4 to 24 with $0D, blanks them, writes "TODAYS TOP  DARKMEN" ($11A8) to $CD22 in colour 7, then for each of the five records of the table at $10A3 writes 17 characters to the screen from $CD9B, 80 bytes (two screen rows) apart: the 10 name codes with $67 added (a space gives $3D) and then 7 of the 8 score digits with $8A added. Called by the entry at $0A37 and by title_wait_fire at $0F11.
"YOU HAVE ACHIEVED A HIGH SCORE" and, at $135F, "PLEASE ENTER YOUR NAME".
The byte after the 31 bytes of high_score_text. title_idle stores 0 in it at $12C0 just before the name entry loop; no code reads it.

Title-screen step: when the NMI flag is clear and $0A13 holds $58 (set by play_setup at $1A37, so only after a game), calls high_score_check ($1110). If that set $110F it runs the name entry: sets $0EEA to 0, blanks rows 4 to 24, prints the high-score messages, takes up to eight letters from the key code $0E2F to $CDEF (RETURN ends, DEL deletes), copies the name with read_name_row ($133D) into the table through insert_score ($114F), sets $0B40 and restarts the title tune ($A164, X=$12).

Copies the eight characters of the name typed on the screen at $CDEF-$CDF6 to the name buffer $1357: the code $81 (the cursor) becomes $20 and any other code has $67 taken off. Called by title_idle at $12FC.

The name typed for the high-score table, one code per character ($20 for a space). title_idle fills it with spaces ($127A) and read_name_row ($133D) writes the typed name; title_idle ($1301), insert_name_unused ($1140) and insert_score ($1151) copy it to $10FD.
"PLEASE ENTER YOUR NAME" in screen codes, followed by $1B; title_idle ($124E) draws its first 23 bytes to $CD70.

The key codes of the cheat sequence "BABY AXE MAN" (ASCII, with spaces), ended by $7B. cheat_check ($1385) compares each new key with the entry at $1383; when the whole sequence has been typed it flips $0A11.
How many keys of cheat_code ($1376) cheat_check ($1385) has matched so far; any other key sets it back to 0.
1 while the key that cheat_check ($1385) last accepted is still held, so that one key press counts once; cleared when the key code $0E2F returns to $FF.

Checks the keys typed on the title pages for the cheat sequence "BABY AXE MAN" (cheat_code, $1376). If the last accepted key is still held ($1384 set) it returns until $0E2F is $FF again. A new key must equal entry $1383 of the sequence: a wrong key resets the index, a right one advances it, and when the next entry is $7B the flag $0A11 is flipped and the index reset. Called by the title interrupt at $1580 every frame.

Draws the credits page. Blanks rows 4 to 24 with colour 7 and writes the first nine lines of credits_text ($1675) to the screen, each with $66 added to its codes (a space gives $3D): at $CCCE in colour $0F, at $CCF6, $CD46, $CD96 and $CDBE in colour 7, at $CE5E, $CE86 and $CED6 in colour 5 and at $CF26 in colour 1. The tenth line, "PRESS FIRE TO START", is not drawn by this routine. Called by the entry at $0A31 and by title_wait_fire at $0F17.

Raster interrupt of the title pages, on line $23 (the vector $FFFE is set to it by title_irq_bottom at $1630). Saves A, X and Y in the operands of the LDA, LDX and LDY before its RTI at $15BB-$15BF, acknowledges the video chip, selects multicolour text with the screen at $CC00 and the character set at $C000 ($D018=$30), turns on sprites 0 to 3 (none while $0A5F or $0F41 is not zero), sets the background colours $D021, $D022 and $D023 to 0, $0B and $0B, calls $A242 and the extended-colour routine $1656, runs cheat_check ($1385), sets the border to $0B while the cheat flag $0A11 is set and to 0 otherwise, counts the 16-bit delay $2039/$203A down to 0, and chains to title_irq_bottom ($15C2) on line $FE.

Raster interrupt of the title pages, on line $FE (set by title_setup at $0B0B and by title_irq_top at $15B3). Saves A, X and Y in the operands of the final LDA, LDX and LDY, sets the extended-colour bit through $163F, places sprites 0 to 3 at Y $E5 and X $8C, $A4, $BC and $D4 with pointers $70 to $73 (screen byte $CFF8-$CFFB) and the colours $01, $06 and $0E, reads the keyboard with read_keys ($0E30) into $0E2F, and chains back to title_irq_top ($1523) on line $23.
Sets bit 6 of $D011 (extended colour mode) when $0A5F is not zero and clears it when it is zero; set_ecm ($1656) does the same and also sets multicolour in $D016. Called by title_irq_bottom at $15CB.
Turns extended colour mode on (and multicolour in $D016) when $0A5F is set, off when it is clear.

Credits page text in screen codes: "TM AND COPYRIGHT 1990 UNIVERSAL CITY STUDIOS INC", the licence lines, "CODED BY FINLAY MUNRO", "GRAPHICS BY NOEL HINES", "SONICS BY JONATHAN DUNN", "PRODUCED BY TWILIGHT" and "PRESS FIRE TO START".
Pause: when the key code in $0E2F is $50, sets $1EF2, waits for the key to be released, pressed again and released, then clears $1EF2.

Main loop of play, after play_setup ($1A21). Each pass runs $1FD5 (a bare RTS), redraws the panel's bar ($4449) and figures ($44FD), runs $1A0C and the pause check. Leaves for $4A8F when $1A1E is set, and for the end of the game ($195C, then $0F38) when $0A11 and $43E3 are both zero or when the NMI flag $2038 is set.

Returns A=1 when an enemy stands in the way of a step left, otherwise A=0. For the enemy slots X=1 and 0 it skips a slot whose state $3742,X is 0 or 5, puts the slot's height $3748,X minus $12 in $1829 and goes on when Darkman's height $2658 is equal to it or up to $13 lines below it; the case of Darkman above it continues at $17FD. The slot blocks when its X ($3744,X with $3746,X) is at or up to $13 left of Darkman's $2657/$2659. Called by the player code before a step left, at $27B0, $2A16, $2BDF and $2EC9.
A bare RTS right after a JMP at $17F9-$17FB; no instruction of the traced code branches or jumps to it.

Part of blocked_left ($17CD), reached from its BCC at $17EF when Darkman's height is above the line in $1829. The slot is skipped (jump to $17D8) when $1829 minus $2658 is $1E or more; otherwise the test of the X positions at $1808 follows.
Scratch byte of blocked_left ($17CD) and blocked_right ($182A): the height of the enemy slot being tested minus $12.

Returns A=1 when an enemy stands in the way of a step right, otherwise A=0. The same test as blocked_left ($17CD) for the other side: the enemy slot X (state not 0 or 5) must be level with Darkman by the height line in $1829, and its X must be at or up to $13 right of Darkman's $2657/$2659. Called by the player code at $280E, $2A50, $2C19 and $2EEB before a step right.
A bare RTS right after a JMP at $1855-$1857; no instruction of the traced code branches or jumps to it.

Part of blocked_right ($182A), reached from its BCC at $184C when Darkman's height is above the line in $1829: the slot is skipped (jump to $1835) when $1829 minus $2658 is $1E or more, otherwise the test of the X positions at $1865 follows.

Lengths of the 56 diagonal lines that wipe_screen ($18C5) clears, each one less than the number of cells on the line: they rise from 0 to $12, stay at $12 for 22 steps and fall to 2 ($1886-$18BD). The two bytes after them are not read.
The last two bytes after wipe_lengths ($1886), 1 and 0, which end its falling run but are never read: wipe_screen takes only the 56 entries $1886-$18BD.
Number of further cells to clear on the current diagonal of wipe_screen ($18C5), after the one being cleared.
Screen address of the first cell of the current diagonal of wipe_screen ($18C5), low byte first.
Set to 1 by wipe_screen ($18C5) and cleared by game_over at $197A; irq_top reads it at $1E54 and keeps the sprites off while it is set.

Wipes the play screen with a diagonal sweep and returns. It sets the wipe flag $18C3 and the pause flag $1EF2 to 1. For each of 56 steps X it takes a length from the table $1886, then clears one more than that many screen cells in both screens ($CC00 and $C800), stepping 39 bytes (one cell down and one to the left) from a start cell that moves along row 0 and then down the right edge ($18C1/$18C2), pausing $32 ($2027) after each step. It clears $1EF2 at the end. Called by game_over ($195C) and by mask_setup.
Holds the X register of wipe_screen ($18C5), saved at $1910: the immediate operand of the LDX at $191B.
Holds the Y register of wipe_screen ($18C5), saved at $1913: the immediate operand of the LDY at $191D.

The second half of wipe_screen ($18C5), after the pause. For the first 39 steps (X below $27) it moves the start cell one place to the right along row 0 ($18C1/$18C2 plus 1) and for the rest one row down (plus $28), going back to $18DF for each of the 56 diagonals. When all 56 are done it clears the pause flag $1EF2 and returns.
End of play: tidies up ($18C5), blanks the screen, silences the sound ($B828), turns the sprites off, switches to a text screen at $CC00 and clears the key code.

The end of game_over ($195C). After the last of six pauses it turns on extended colour mode, swaps the character data back with swap_font_a ($4D8B), clears both screens to 0, redraws the bottom rows through draw_bottom_rows ($203C) and returns.
"GAME OVER" in screen codes.
When the resident flag $0A11 is not zero and the key code $0E2F is $20 (the space bar), sets the end-of-play flag $1A1E to 1. Called by the play loop at $17AA.
Set to 1 to end play: by skip_key_check ($1A0C) and by exit_touch_test ($4586). play_setup and mask_setup ($592D) clear it, and the play loop leaves for end_of_level ($4A8F) when it is set.

How far the playfield has scrolled, low byte first. scroll_step ($2066) adds the scroll speed to it; the object list read by objects_step ($3297) and the enemy list read at $3190 are compared with it, and so is the list read by the unused scroll_stop_test_unused ($4087).

Start of play, called by play_loop at $179E: blacks the screen (extended colour mode on, $D011 bit 6), turns sprites off, clears the end-of-play flag $1A1E, pauses through $2027, banks the ROMs out and selects video bank 3 with $D018=$34, then sets up the play screen and interrupts.
Copies 13 pages (3,328 bytes) from $747B to $B000, 256 bytes at a time through the pointers $E1/$E2 and $DF/$E0, and then calls $B0C8 in the sound driver. Called once by play_setup at $1B38.
Copies 19 pages (4,864 bytes) from $80B4 to $A000, 256 bytes at a time through the pointers $E1/$E2 and $DF/$E0. Called once by title_setup at $0ABE.
Copies 256 bytes from $1C42 to $FE00-$FEFF, which lie in the panel's bitmap (see panel_bitmap_7 at $FDF0). Called once by play_setup at $1B44.
256 bytes of pixel patterns that load_panel_bitmap ($1C36) copies to $FE00.
Which screen matrix is shown: 1 for the one at $CC00 and 0 for the one at $C800. select_screen ($1FA4) turns it into $D018 and scroll_step ($2066) flips it after each whole-character step.

Raster interrupt 3 of 4 in play. Sets the screen-matrix bits of $D018 to 3 (screen at $CC00) and ORs $D011 with $4F, which turns on extended colour mode; blacks the border and the sprite multicolours, counts down $29F4 and $29F3, and reads joystick port 2 ($DC00) into $203B whenever $29F3 is zero. Then selects the character set at $E000 ($D018 low bits $08), sets the next raster line to 205 and chains to $1DBF. The final LDA, LDX and LDY get their operands from the stores at the top: the saved registers are restored by self-modified code.
Holds the A register saved by irq_panel ($1D43): the immediate operand of the LDA at $1DB6.
Holds the X register saved by irq_panel ($1D43): the immediate operand of the LDX at $1DB8.
Holds the Y register saved by irq_panel ($1D43): the immediate operand of the LDY at $1DBA.

A countdown that irq_panel ($1D43) takes 1 from on every second frame (when $1DBE has just become 1) until it reaches 0. The mask game's interrupt irq_mask_1 ($5A7A) counts it down in the same way at $5AC4. No traced code sets it above 0.
Flipped between 0 and 1 by irq_panel ($1D43) on every frame (and by the mask game's interrupt irq_mask_1 at $5ABF); the countdown $1DBD only moves on when it has just become 1.

Raster interrupt 4 of 4 in play. After a run of NOPs that times the write to the raster line, sets bit 5 (bitmap) of $D011 and multicolour in $D016, blacks the border, sets the next interrupt for line 10 at $1E21, clears extended colour mode again, and unless the game is paused ($1EF2) calls $41EF, $4636 and $2066.
Holds the A register saved by irq_bottom ($1DBF): the immediate operand of the LDA at $1E1A.
Holds the X register saved by irq_bottom ($1DBF): the immediate operand of the LDX at $1E1C.
Holds the Y register saved by irq_bottom ($1DBF): the immediate operand of the LDY at $1E1E.

Raster interrupt 1 of 4 in play, on line 10. Acknowledges the video chip, sets the fine horizontal scroll from $1EF3, sets the colour mode ($1656) and the screen matrix ($1FA4), and turns sprites on unless $18C3 hides them. Then runs the play subsystems ($265E, $354A, $3725, and while not paused $4140 and $3190, then $3297), places Darkman's three sprites (0, 1 and 2) at the position held in $2657, $2659 and $2658, the second 21 lines lower, and colours them. Calls $4586 and $45C9 when not paused, and chains to $1EF4 on line 80.
Holds the A register saved by irq_top ($1E21): the immediate operand of the LDA at $1EEB.
Holds the X register saved by irq_top ($1E21): the immediate operand of the LDX at $1EED.
Holds the Y register saved by irq_top ($1E21): the immediate operand of the LDY at $1EEF.
1 while the game is paused ($1777) and while wipe_screen ($18C5) runs; the interrupts skip the moving parts of the game while it is set.
The fine horizontal scroll, 0 to 7, that the raster interrupts write to the low bits of $D016. scroll_step ($2066) lowers it by the scroll speed.

Raster interrupt 2 of 4 in play, on line 80. Sets the scroll again and the background multicolours $0B and $0F, calls $1F40, plays the music and effects ($B176), reads the keyboard ($0E30) into $0E2F, and chains to $1D43 on line 198.
Holds the A register saved by irq_2 ($1EF4): the immediate operand of the LDA at $1F39.
Holds the X register saved by irq_2 ($1EF4): the immediate operand of the LDX at $1F3B.
Holds the Y register saved by irq_2 ($1EF4): the immediate operand of the LDY at $1F3D.

Moves one of Darkman's sprites 8 pixels sideways on each call. When $2768 is not zero it moves sprite 0 ($D000, with the ninth bit in $D010 bit 0), otherwise when $2F67 is not zero it moves sprite 1 ($D002, bit 1); it goes right when the facing $273D is 0 and left when it is not, and returns at once when both are zero. Called by irq_2 at $1F1E.
Selects the screen matrix through $D018: $30 (screen at $CC00) when $1D42 is set, $20 (screen at $C800) when it is clear, with the character set at $C000 either way. Two screens to flip between.
Mixes CIA 1's timer A, both bytes, with the previous result in $1FD4 and rotates it: a random number in $1FD4.

The branch offset of the BCS at $1FC5. random ($1FB5) stores the low three bits of CIA 1 timer A here, and since the carry is always set the branch skips that many of the nine ROL A instructions at $1FC7-$1FCF, so the number is rotated 2 to 9 times, a different amount each time.
The last number made by random ($1FB5).

Starts with RTS, so it returns at once. The bytes after it would read CIA 2 port A bit 2, return when it is set, and when it is clear pull three bytes off the stack (PLA three times), set the interrupt flag and jump to $0810; nothing reaches them while the RTS is there. Called from $0A29, $0EEC, $17A1, $4A92 and $4C4C.

Code right after the RTS of disabled_check ($1FD5); nothing calls it or jumps to it ($1FDE is only its own branch target). It reads $DD00 and returns when bit 2 is set; when bit 2 is clear it takes three bytes off the stack, sets the interrupt flag and jumps to $0810, the JMP $0B1B left in the boot's entry stub at $080D. In level 1, $0B1B is the middle of the instruction LDA #$FF at $0B1A, so this path is a leftover.

Stores A in both screen matrices, $CC00-$CFFF and $C800-$CBFF (1,024 bytes each). Called by title_setup ($0AAD), type_briefing ($0F5A), game_over ($19A4 and $19FB), play_setup ($1B30), subject_screen ($571A) and mask_setup ($58C8, at $59DA and $5A05).
Stores A in the screen matrix $C800-$CBFF (1,024 bytes). Called by subject_screen ($5785) and mask_setup ($58C8, at $5A0A).

Stores A in colour RAM, $D800-$DBFF (1,024 bytes). Called by title_setup ($0AB2), type_briefing ($0F5F), game_over ($19A9), play_setup ($1B35), subject_screen ($571F) and mask_setup ($58C8, at $59DF).
A pause: an inner loop of A passes run A times (Y and X both start from A). Called 38 times across the level, among them six times in a row with A=$FF from $0A3A, the pause between the attract pages.
Non-maskable interrupt: sets the flag $2038 to 1 and returns.
Set to 1 by every NMI ($2030); cleared and polled by the code that waits on it.

A 16-bit countdown, low byte first ($203A is the high byte). title_wait_fire ($0EFD) loads it with $0232 after a page change, title_irq_top ($1523) takes 1 from it every frame down to 0, and title_wait_fire only changes the page when the high byte $203A is 0.

Joystick port 2 as last read: by irq_panel ($1D87) in play, by title_irq_top ($1552) on the title and by the code at $5AA8; bit 4 clear is fire. $0A9E, $1A71 and $58EB set it to $FF (nothing pressed), and the enemy attack code (at $3B2D, $3BA7, $3BD9, $3C25 and $3C82) changes it when it hurts Darkman: all directions and fire released at $3B2D, a push to the right or the left (bit 3 or bit 2 cleared) at the others.

Copies 200 bytes from $6D95 to colour RAM $DAF7 and 200 bytes from $6CCD to the screen matrix $CEF7 (from column 39 of row 18 to column 38 of row 23), then clears the 40 bytes of row 24 at $CFC0 and at $DBC0. Called by game_over at $19FE, play_setup at $1B3B and mask_setup ($58C8) at $5A10.
Address of the next map column to draw, low byte first. It starts at $6E71 and draw_new_column ($2269) adds 1 on every second call; scroll_step ($2066) stops the scroll when it reaches $6EF9.

Pixels the playfield scrolls on each step of scroll_step ($2066): 2 or 0. player_move ($265E) sets it to 0 each frame, or to 2 when advance_flag is set and Darkman is at X $D5 or beyond; player_control ($284D, $289E), player_fall ($2A8A, $2AC9) and player_jump ($2C47, $2C98) set it to 2 when a step reaches the right limit and to 0 when a step is undone in a solid tile; play_setup ($1B54) and scroll_step at the end of the map clear it.
Set to 1 by scroll_step ($2066) when the scroll has reached the end of the map; read by exit_marker_step ($354A) and exit_touch_test ($4586).
1 once copy_screen ($2120) has copied the screen for the current scroll step, and 0 again after shift_colour_left ($21FA); scroll_step ($2066) does not copy while it is 1.
Scratch byte of scroll_step ($2066) for the wrapped fine scroll.
The sum of the scroll speeds, low byte first, added by scroll_step ($2066). No traced code reads it.

Scrolls the playfield one step left on every call, unless $4079 is set. When $205F is $6E and $205E is $F9 or more (the end of the map) it clears the speed $2060, sets the end flag $2061 and returns. Otherwise it lowers the fine scroll $1EF3 by the speed $2060, adding 8 when that goes below 0 (a whole-character step). It adds the speed to the scroll position $1A1F/$1A20 and to the distance $2064/$2065, moves both enemy slots' X ($3744 and $3745 with $3746 and $3747) left by it and switches a slot off if its X goes below 0. Without a whole-character step it copies the screen with $2120 once ($2062 clear); with one it calls $21FA and flips the screen flag $1D42. Called by irq_bottom at $1E17.
Holds the Y flag of scroll_step ($2066), saved at $20C4: the immediate operand of the LDY at $20C7. It is 1 when the fine scroll has wrapped round and the screen must be shifted a whole character.

The rest of scroll_step ($2066). It moves both enemy slots' X positions ($3744/$3746 and $3745/$3747) left by the scroll speed, setting the slot's state ($3742 or $3743) to 0 when the position goes below 0. It adds the speed to the total $2064/$2065 and, when the saved flag is 1, shifts colour RAM left through shift_colour_left ($21FA) and flips the screen flag $1D42.
3 zero bytes after with no type between code ($211D): padding that no traced code reads.

Sets $2062 and copies rows 1 to 16 of the shown screen to the hidden one shifted one character left (38 bytes a row, columns 1-38 to 0-37): from $CC00 to $C800 when $1D42 is set, from $C800 to $CC00 when it is clear. The copy behind the screen flip in $1FA4.

Clears $2062, shifts colour RAM one cell left in rows 1 to 16 (38 bytes per row, for example $D829-$D84E to $D828-$D84D), and then calls draw_new_column ($2269). Called by scroll_step at $2111 on each whole-character step.
0 or 1: which half of a two-character-wide map cell the next column is. draw_new_column ($2269) flips it and draw_map_cell ($22C0) adds it to the table index.

Draws the next map column at column 38 of rows 1 to 16. It flips the half-column $2268 and, when that becomes 0, adds 1 to the map position $205E/$205F. It points $10/$11 at the map, $12/$13 at the screen that is not shown ($C84E when $1D42 is set, else $CC4E) and $14/$15 at colour RAM $D84E, and calls draw_map_cell ($22C0) eight times, adding $AE (the map's row length) to $10/$11 after each. Called by shift_colour_left at $2264.

Draws one map cell as two characters, one above the other. The map byte at ($10) times 2 plus the half-column $2268 picks the top character from $6BB3 (written to ($12)) and the bottom character from $6C51 (written to ($12)+$28); the colour of each, from the table $BF00, goes to ($14) and ($14)+$28. It then adds $50 to $12/$13 and $14/$15 and $AE to $10/$11. Called eight times by draw_new_column.

The first 170 characters of the first screen: draw_first_screen ($2608) copies them to $CC00-$CCA9 (rows 0 to 3 and the first 10 characters of row 4 of the screen matrix) and takes each one's colour from the table at $BF00.
The second 170 characters of the first screen, for the screen matrix at $CCAA-$CD53 (the rest of row 4 up to column 19 of row 8), copied by draw_first_screen ($2608).
The third 170 characters of the first screen, for $CD54-$CDFD (from column 20 of row 8 to column 29 of row 12), copied by draw_first_screen ($2608).

The last 170 characters of the first screen, for $CDFE-$CEA7 (from column 30 of row 12 to the end of row 16), copied by draw_first_screen ($2608). The 80 bytes after it, to $2607, are zero and nothing reads them.

Fills the first screen. Copies 170 bytes from each of the tables $2310, $23BA, $2464 and $250E to the screen matrix at $CC00, $CCAA, $CD54 and $CDFE, and writes each character's colour, from the table $BF00, to colour RAM $D800, $D8AA, $D954 and $D9FE. Called once by play_setup at $1B41.

Darkman's state, the index into the table at $2645: 0 nothing, 1 standing and walking, 2 falling, 3 jumping, 4 climbing, 5 punch, 6 crouch, 7 strike. player_move ($265E) calls the routine of the current state.

Eight routine addresses, low byte first, one for each state of $2644: 0 is player_idle ($26D4, an RTS), 1 player_control ($276B), 2 player_fall ($2A0A), 3 player_jump ($2B69), 4 player_climb ($2D14), 5 player_punch ($2E11), 6 player_crouch ($2F68) and 7 player_strike ($2E6F). player_move ($265E) copies the one for the current state into the JSR at $26CB.

Darkman's X position (low byte) as it was when player_move ($265E) began this frame, stored at $26A8. The state routines copy it back to $2657 when a step would end in a solid tile (at $2890, $2ABB, $2C8A and $2F35); player_strike also uses it at $2F35 to undo a step past the left edge or the right limit.
Darkman's Y position as it was when player_move ($265E) began this frame, stored at $26B1. No code reads it.
Darkman's horizontal position, low byte (with $2659 the ninth bit), written to sprites 0-2 by $1E21.
Darkman's vertical position, written to sprites 0 and 2 by $1E21; sprite 1 sits 21 lines below.
Ninth bit of Darkman's horizontal position.

A second copy of Darkman's X position (low byte) from the start of the frame (stored at $26AB). player_control, player_fall and player_jump copy it back to $2657 when a step takes him past the left edge ($1E) or the right limit ($265C/$265D); player_strike uses $2655 for that instead.
The ninth bit of Darkman's X position from the start of the frame (stored at $26B7). The state routines copy it back to $2659 together with the low byte whenever they undo a step.
The low byte of the right limit of Darkman's X position, set by player_move ($265E) each frame: $2D normally and $D2 while advance_flag ($3638) is set.
The high byte of the right limit of Darkman's X position: 1 normally and 0 while advance_flag ($3638) is set, so the limit is $012D or $00D2.
Moves Darkman; skipped while paused. Begins by testing his position against the right edge ($D5 with the ninth bit) when $3638 is set.
The operand of the JSR at $26CB: the address of the routine for Darkman's current state, low byte at $26CC and high byte at $26CD, stored by player_move ($265E) from state_table.

The end of player_move ($265E): calls player_draw ($2FC7) to put Darkman's sprite pointers into the tables, then returns. Also reached by the branch at $2661 while the game is paused and by the jump at $268A, which ends the step when advance_flag is set and he is at X $D5 or beyond (he is then moved 2 back and the scroll speed $2060 set to 2).
2 zero bytes after with no type between code ($26D2): padding that no traced code reads.
State 0 of state_table ($2645): an RTS, so in this state player_move ($265E) moves nothing. No code in the file sets the state to 0.

Index of the current step of an animation: 0 to 17 for the walk, used by walk_anim_left ($26FB) and walk_anim_right ($271C), and 0 to 11 for the climb, used by climb_frame_a ($2DCF) and climb_frame_b ($2DF0).
The frames of the walk to the left, three each of $9D to $A2, read by walk_anim_left ($26FB); player_control takes the first one at $27A0 when the stick is pushed left.
The frames of the walk to the right, three each of $97 to $9C, read by walk_anim_right ($271C); player_control takes the first one at $27FE when the stick is pushed right.
Flipped by walk_anim_left, walk_anim_right, climb_frame_a and climb_frame_b on every call; the animation moves on when it becomes 1.

Steps the walk to the left. Flips $26FA and, every second call, moves the index $26D5 on through 18 values (back to 0 after 17); then puts the entry $26D6 plus the index into Darkman's frame $2FC3. The 18 entries are three each of $9D to $A2. Called by the player code at $28A9 when $2769 is set.

The same for the walk to the right: flips $26FA, advances $26D5 through 18 values every second call and puts the entry $26E8 plus the index in $2FC3. The 18 entries are three each of $97 to $9C. Called by the player code at $28B4 when $276A is set.
Which way Darkman faces: 0 for right and 1 for left.
The column that tile_at_probe ($309D) left in Y for the point at Darkman's feet; stored by the player code at $28DF.
1 while Darkman is crouching: set by start_attack ($2979), cleared by play_setup, by player_strike ($2E93, $2EC1) and by player_crouch ($2FBE) when the stick comes up. player_draw ($2FC7) reads it.
Countdown that, while it is not zero, keeps start_attack ($2979) from starting a crouch or a strike; start_attack counts it down.
Countdown that, while it is not zero, keeps start_attack ($2979) from starting a punch; start_attack counts it down.
Countdown that, while it is not zero, keeps start_jump ($293F) from starting a jump; the player code counts it down at $277E.

Sets the three sprite pointers $2FC4, $2FC5 and $2FC6 to $92, $B6 and $C0 when Darkman faces right ($273D zero) and to $93, $B7 and $C1 when he faces left. Called by start_attack at $29AE and by the code at $2FAE.

Set to 9 when start_attack ($2979) starts a punch, counted down by player_punch ($2E11) and cleared by play_setup. shift_attack_sprite ($1F40), player_draw ($2FC7) and enemy_hit_check ($421F) read it.
Set to 1 by player_control ($276B) at $27EA when Darkman has taken a step left and cleared at the start of every pass; the walk animation walk_anim_left ($26FB) is called at $28A9 while it is 1.

Set to 1 by player_control ($276B) at $2857 and $285F when Darkman has taken a step right and cleared at the start of every pass; the walk animation walk_anim_right ($271C) is called at $28B4 while it is 1.

Reads the stick for Darkman: clears the walk flags $2769 and $276A and the stun turn counter $312D, rounds his height in $2658 to the bottom of a character row (ORA #$07), counts down $2742, clears $2A08, $2A09 and the strike counter $2F67, then tests left ($203B and $DC00 bit 2) and the other directions to choose a move.

Starts a climb when the tile under Darkman's feet column ($273E) is 1 or 2 (a ladder): state 4, Y lowered by 2, $2DB6 and the drawing state $2B68 set to 1; any other tile jumps to start_jump ($293F). Nothing jumps to it: the jump at $2918 sits in front of it.

Reached by the jump at $2918 from the player code when the stick is pushed up. When the jump delay $2742 is zero it starts a jump: sets the state $2644 to 3, the drawing state $2B68 to 3 and the step $2B67 to 0, puts the falling frame in with fall_frame ($2CC3) and returns. Otherwise it goes to $2955, which tests the stick's down bit and in both cases continues at start_attack ($2979).

A second way into state 4: when the flag $2FC2 is zero and the tile at ($8D),y is 3 or 4 it sets state 4 and the drawing state 1; otherwise it goes to start_attack ($2979). Nothing jumps to it and $2FC2 is never written.

Starts a crouch, a strike or a punch, reached by the branch at $295A and the jump at $295C. While $2740 is zero and the stick is pushed down, fire (bit 4 of $203B clear) starts the strike (state $2644 to 7, $2F67 to $0E, strike_frames $2E30, sound effect 0 through $B0EE) and no fire starts the crouch (state 6, $273F to 1, crouch_frames $2743, $2B68 to 6). Otherwise, when $2741 is zero and fire is pressed, it starts the punch (state 5, $2768 to 9, punch_frames $2D91, $2B68 to 0, sound effect 0). A non-zero $2740 or $2741 is counted down first. With the stick centred (low four bits $0F) it shows the standing frame ($29F5).
The screen code under Darkman, stored by player_control ($276B) at $2867 and $287D while it tests whether a step is blocked. No code reads it. The two zero bytes after it, to $29F2, are not used.

Countdown set to 3 by player_hurt ($43E4); the leap code ($3B32, $3BAC, $3BDE), enemy_punch ($3C2A) and enemy_punch_left ($3C87) store 4 here just before calling it. irq_panel counts it down and reads the joystick only when it is zero or has just reached zero.

Counts down by 1 on every frame in irq_panel ($1D43). The leap code (enemy_leap, $3A15) sets it to $0A each time it hurts Darkman and does not hurt him again while it is not zero (tests at $3B03, $3B8D and $3BBF).
Puts the standing frame in Darkman's frame $2FC3: $9A when he faces right ($273D zero) and $A0 when he faces left. Called by play_setup at $1AE2, by start_attack at $29EC and by the code at $2AF7.
Cleared by the player code at $2789 on every pass and by player_fall at $2A0C, and set to 1 by enemy_hit_check ($421F) when a blow lands; no traced code reads it.
Cleared by the player code at $278C on every pass and set to 1 by enemy_hit_check ($421F) when a blow lands; no traced code reads it.

State 2 of state_table ($2645): Darkman falling. Clears hit_flag_a, moves him 2 left or right with the stick (checking blocked_left and blocked_right and the same limits as player_control, undoing the step in a solid tile), adds 2 to his Y (plus the carry left by the comparisons) and then sets the state back to 1 and shows the standing frame through stand_frame ($29F5), so player_control decides again each frame whether he is still in the air.

When Darkman's Y ($2658) is below $71 it shows the falling frame (fall_frame, $2CC3) and returns, otherwise it goes back to the state change at $2AF2. Nothing jumps or calls into it; it follows the RTS of player_fall.
Puts $7A (facing right) or $7B (facing left) in Darkman's frame $2FC3. Nothing calls it; stand_frame ($29F5) uses $9A and $A0 instead.

The height changes of a jump, 39 pairs of bytes (78 bytes). player_jump ($2B69) adds the first byte of each pair, as a signed step, to Darkman's Y; the second byte ($FF or 0, its sign) is never read. The steps go from -4 to 4 and add up to 0, so he lands at the height he left.

Position in the table of jump heights at $2B19, or of strike heights at $2E55, two bytes a step, used by player_jump ($2B69) and player_strike ($2E6F); start_jump ($293F), start_attack ($2979) and player_crouch ($2F68) set it to 0.
When it is not zero player_draw ($2FC7) draws that state instead of $2644 and clears it. start_jump, start_attack, the fall code at $290A and player_jump (at $2B7E and $2BC5) set it.

State 3 of state_table ($2645): Darkman jumping. Adds the entry of jump_arc ($2B19) at step $2B67 to his Y and moves the step on by 2; after step $4E it returns to state 1 with the falling frame. From step $29 on it tests the three cells under his feet and ends the jump on a solid tile (code 2 to $0D). Then it moves him 2 left or right with the stick, undoes the step in a solid tile and counts down the strike counter $2F67 with strike_frames ($2E30).
Puts the falling frame in Darkman's frame $2FC3: $F8 when he faces right ($273D zero) and $F9 when he faces left. Called by the player code at $290D, $2951, $2B02, $2B8E, $2BD5 and $2CBF.

The second half of a copy of climb_frame_a ($2DCF), without its first instruction: flips $26FA, steps $26D5 through 12 values and sets the frame $2FC3 from climb_frames_up ($2DB7). Nothing calls or jumps to it.
Sixteen 16-bit values, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2 and so on up to 7, 7. Nothing reads them.

State 4 of state_table ($2645): Darkman on a ladder. Sets the jump delay $2742 to 10, moves him up 1 line with the stick up (climb_frame_a) or down 1 with the stick down (climb_frame_b), and keeps the state while the cell under him is a ladder tile (1 to 4). Otherwise it returns to state 1 with a standing frame and $2740 set to 4, and, if he was climbing up, moves him 2 lines down (adds 2 to $2658). The only code that sets state 4 is unreached ($291B and $295F).

Sets the three sprite pointers $2FC4, $2FC5 and $2FC6 for the punch: $90, $B4 and $BE when Darkman faces right ($273D zero) and $91, $B5 and $BF when he faces left. Called by start_attack at $29D1 and by the code at $2E2C.

1 while Darkman climbs up and 0 while he climbs down, set by player_climb ($2D14) at $2D2B and $2D46 (and to 1 by the unreached ladder_start_unused at $2938) and read at $2D82 when he leaves the ladder.
The 12 sprite pointers of the climb up: $94, $95, $96, $95 three times each. climb_frame_a ($2DCF) takes one by the index $26D5.
The 12 sprite pointers of the climb down: $96, $95, $94, $95 three times each. climb_frame_b ($2DF0) takes one by the index $26D5.

Flips $26FA and, on every second call, moves the index $26D5 on through 12 values (back to 0 after 11); then puts the entry of climb_frames_up ($2DB7) at that index in Darkman's frame $2FC3. Called by player_climb at $2D2E.
The same as climb_frame_a ($2DCF) for the climb down: flips $26FA, steps $26D5 through 12 values and puts the entry of climb_frames_down ($2DC3) in $2FC3. Called by player_climb at $2D49.

State 5 of state_table ($2645): Darkman punching. While the punch counter $2768 is not zero it counts it down and sets the punch sprites with punch_frames ($2D91). When it has run out the state holds until fire ($203B bit 4) is released, then returns to state 1 with the punch delay $2741 set to 6.

Sets the three sprite pointers $2FC4, $2FC5 and $2FC6 for the strike: $8C, $A3 and $B0 when Darkman faces right ($273D zero) and $8D, $B1 and $BB when he faces left. Called by start_attack at $299B and by the code at $2CA4, $2F4A and $2F7E.

The height changes of a strike, 13 pairs of bytes: the first byte of each pair is a signed step (-6, -5 up to 6, rising and then falling) that player_strike ($2E6F) adds to Darkman's Y; the second byte is never read. The steps add up to 0.

State 7 of state_table ($2645): Darkman's flying strike. Adds the entry of strike_arc ($2E55) at step $2B67 to his Y and moves the step on by 2; at step $1A, or from step $0F when the code at the probe offset plus $40 is from 1 to $13, the state returns to 1, with $2740 set to 10 and the crouch flag cleared. He moves 2 pixels a frame the way he faces, undoing the step in a wall, shows the walk frame $9B or $A1 and counts down the strike counter $2F67 with strike_frames ($2E30).
Set to $0A by player_jump ($2B69) and player_strike ($2E6F) when the strike counter $2F67 has run out, and counted down to 0 by them on the following frames. No other code reads it.

Set to $0E when start_attack ($2979) or player_crouch ($2F68) starts a strike, counted down by player_jump and player_strike, and cleared by the player code at $278F on every pass, by play_setup and when a jump or strike ends. shift_attack_sprite ($1F40), player_draw ($2FC7) and enemy_hit_check ($421F) read it.

State 6 of state_table ($2645): Darkman crouching. With fire pressed ($203B bit 4 clear) it starts the strike: state 7, step $2B67 to 0, strike counter $2F67 to $0E, strike_frames ($2E30) and sound effect 0 through $B0EE. While the stick is held down it turns him with left or right (unless he is stunned) and shows the crouch frames (crouch_frames, $2743); when the stick comes up it returns to state 1 with $2740 set to 10 and the crouch flag cleared.
Always 0. Only the unreached code at $295F reads it.

The sprite pointer for Darkman's body, set by walk_anim_left, walk_anim_right, stand_frame, fall_frame, climb_frame_a, climb_frame_b, player_control ($27A3, $2801), player_climb ($2D77, $2D7F) and player_strike ($2F1B), and written to the sprite tables by player_draw ($2FC7).

The three sprite pointers of the punch, strike and crouch: for sprite 2, sprite 0 and sprite 1. crouch_frames, punch_frames and strike_frames set them and player_draw ($2FC7) writes them to the sprite tables.

Writes Darkman's three sprite pointers into both screens' tables ($CFF8-$CFFA and $CBF8-$CBFA). The state drawn is $2B68 (which it then clears) when that is not zero, otherwise $2644. For states 2 and 3 sprite 2 gets $2FC3 and sprites 0 and 1 get that plus 2 and plus 4; for state 4 sprite 2 gets $2FC3, sprite 0 that plus $24 and sprite 1 that plus $2E. In the other states, while $2768, $273F or $2F67 is not zero, the pointers come from $2FC4 (sprite 2), $2FC5 (sprite 0) and $2FC6 (sprite 1); otherwise sprite 0 gets $2FC3, sprite 1 that plus $0D and sprite 2 that minus $17. Called by player_move at $26CE.
The low byte of the X position for tile_at_probe ($309D); the high byte is in $3065.
The Y position for tile_at_probe ($309D).
The high byte of the X position for tile_at_probe ($309D).
7 zero bytes after between data records that no label reaches (after probe_x_hi) ($3066): padding that no traced code reads.
The screen address of each of the 23 rows of the screen matrix at $CC00 ($CC00, $CC28, ... $CF70), low byte first, read by tile_at_probe ($309D).
The row address that tile_at_probe ($309D) last took from the table, stored there (also in $8D/$8E). enemy_shoot_part_2 reads it at $4118 and $4120 for the shot's row pointer.

Returns in A the screen code under the point set by the callers: the row is ($3064 minus $24) divided by 8, which picks the row address from the table $306D (also kept in $8D/$8E and in $309B/$309C), minus $0400 when the screen at $C800 is the one in use ($1D42 clear); the column is $3063 divided by 8, plus $20 when $3065 is not zero, minus 3. Y is left set to that column. Called by probe_player ($34E0), probe_enemy_right ($386F), probe_enemy_left ($38A4) and the code at $3129 and $4115.

Sets the point for tile_at_probe ($309D) in front of Darkman: X is his $2657/$2659 rounded down to a multiple of 8, plus 8, plus the fine scroll $1EF3 (minus 16 when he faces left), Y is $2658 plus $16. Returns the screen code there in A. Nothing calls it.

Counts how often player_control ($276B) reaches the stun test at $28B7 in one pass while Darkman is stunned ($29F3 not zero): at 1 his facing is flipped and the step is tested again from $2862; at 2 the facing is flipped back and the pass goes on. Cleared at the start of every pass.

The enemies of the level: 14 records of 7 bytes, each a scroll position (low byte, high byte) and then the side (0 left, 1 right), the state, the slot (0 or 1), the kind and twice the energy. Read through the pointer $87/$88 by enemy_spawn_check ($3190), which starts the enemy when the scroll position $1A1F/$1A20 reaches the position.

Starts the next enemy from the record that the pointer $87/$88 points at (enemy_spawn_table, $312E) once the scroll position $1A1F/$1A20 has reached the record's position. It clears the object slots' states $33EA and $33EB and sprites 3 and 4's Y ($D007, $D009), then fills the enemy slot named in byte 4: state (byte 3), side (byte 2: X $000F or $016E with the direction), Y $78, kind (byte 5) and energy (byte 6 halved), clears the count and the hurt flag, and moves the pointer on by 7. Called by irq_top at $1E79.
The list that objects_step ($3297) reads: 22 records of 4 bytes, a position (low byte, high byte) and the types for object slots 0 and 1. $81/$82 points at the next record.

The sprite pointer of sprite 7, taken from the table $3518 by exit_marker_step ($354A).
Index into the table $3518 of sprite 7's frames, stepped by exit_marker_step ($354A).

Countdown of exit_marker_step ($354A) when it shows sprite 7 at the edge; reloaded with $FF at 0, and at that moment it plays sound effect 3 (X = $0C) unless the game is paused.
X position of sprite 7 at the end of the map, low byte then the ninth bit, read by exit_marker_step ($354A) and exit_touch_test ($4586).

Countdown that delays exit_marker_step ($354A); play_setup sets it to 5.

Per-frame step of sprite 7 (position $D00E/$D00F, pointer $CFFF and $CBFF). Otherwise, when the end flag $2061 is set, it shows the sprite at $3546/$3547/$3548 with the pointer $6F, adding 1 to its Y up to $8A and keeping its X at $01E or more while the ninth bit $3547 is clear and at $128 or less while it is set. When neither holds, it puts the sprite at X $11E and Y $3C with the pointer $3516 and colour 6, counts $3545 down (at 0, reloaded with $FF, it plays sound effect 3, X = $0C, unless paused), clears $4079 and sets $3638 to 1. Called by irq_top at $1E6B.
Holds the X register of exit_marker_step ($354A), stored at $3611: the immediate operand of the LDX at $3619, which restores it after the sound call.
Holds the Y register of exit_marker_step ($354A), stored at $360E: the immediate operand of the LDY at $361B.

The end of exit_marker_step ($354A), reached by the jump at $3601, by the branch at $360C when the game is paused, and, after the sound call, by falling through. Puts sprite 7's Y at $3C, clears the scroll stop $4079 and sets advance_flag ($3638) to 1. The code at $362D, reached from $357C when an enemy slot is in use, puts sprite 7's Y at 1 and sets $4079 to 1.

Set to 1 by exit_marker_step ($354A) when no enemy is in play and sprite 7 shows at the edge, 0 otherwise; it keeps its value while the delay $3549 counts down. player_move ($265E) reads it: when it is set, Darkman reaching X $D5 makes the playfield scroll and his limit ($265C/$265D) is $00D2, otherwise it is $012D. player_control ($276B) reads it at $2850: when it is set and Darkman is held at his limit, it still marks a step right ($276A).
Places the two enemies' sprites: sprites 3 and 4 for the first (from $3744, $3746 and $3748) and 5 and 6 for the second, each pair stacked 21 lines apart, and sets their colours.
Scratch byte of place_enemies ($3639): the size of a negative enemy step, which it subtracts from the X of the upper sprite.
Calls $384E and $421F for each of two slots (X=0, 1), unless paused, then $3639.

State of enemy slot 0 ($3742) and slot 1 ($3743). 0 means the slot is empty, 1 waiting, 2 walking left, 3 walking right, 4 throwing, 5 dying, 6 punching right, 7 punching left and 8 leaping. enemy_frame ($384E) runs the routine of the state from enemy_state_table ($38D9); blocked_left ($17CD) skips a slot in state 0 or 5.
X position of enemy slot 0 ($3744) and slot 1 ($3745), low byte; the ninth bit is in $3746 and $3747. place_enemies ($3639) writes it to the sprite registers.
The ninth bit of the X position of enemy slots 0 and 1 (see enemy_x at $3744).
Y position of enemy slot 0 ($3748) and slot 1 ($3749). place_enemies ($3639) writes it to the upper sprite and 21 lines more to the lower one.
Direction of enemy slots 0 and 1: 0 or 1.

The sprite pointer of the upper sprite of enemy slot 0 ($374C) and slot 1 ($374D). place_enemies ($3639) writes them to $CFFB/$CBFB and $CFFD/$CBFD (sprites 3 and 5). enemy_wind_up_frame ($3F46), enemy_attack_frame ($3F76), the walks and enemy_leap from their frame tables, enemy_dying ($3CAC), enemy_throw ($3D4D) and enemy_leap_hurt ($3B3D) set them.
The sprite pointer of the lower sprite of enemy slot 0 ($374E) and slot 1 ($374F). place_enemies ($3639) writes them to $CFFC/$CBFC and $CFFE/$CBFE (sprites 4 and 6).

Counter of enemy slots 0 and 1, the frame count of the slot's state: enemy_leap, enemy_punch ($3BEC), enemy_punch_left, enemy_dying and enemy_throw count it up, enemy_wait and the walks count it down, and enemy_decide ($3FD2), enemy_spawn_check ($3190), the walks and enemy_damage ($43BF) set it.

Pixels that enemy slot 0 ($3752) and slot 1 ($3753) shift their upper sprite on each frame, as a signed byte ($F8 or $08 in an attack, a throw or a leap blow, otherwise 0); set by every enemy state routine (enemy_leap, enemy_punch ($3BEC), enemy_punch_left, enemy_dying, enemy_throw, enemy_wait, the walks) and by enemy_attack_frame ($3F76), and added by place_enemies ($3639) to the X of the upper sprite only.

Type of enemy slots 0 and 1; 0 or not 0 picks the frames in enemy_wind_up_frame ($3F46), enemy_attack_frame ($3F76), the walks ($3E3A, $3F19) and enemy_dying ($3CB1), and enemy_decide ($3FD2) lets only a kind other than 0 throw.

The step in the walk tables of enemy slot 0 ($3756) and slot 1 ($3757), 0 to 19. enemy_walk_left ($3EA5) and enemy_walk_right ($3DC4) add 1 on each frame that the enemy moves (back to 0 at 20) and read the sprite pointers and step at that index.

Energy of enemy slots 0 and 1. enemy_damage ($43BF) takes 1 from it and starts the dying state 5 when it is already 0. For a leaping enemy (state 8) enemy_hit_check ($421F) takes the 1 itself and sets enemy_hurt, and enemy_leap_hurt ($3B3D) ends the slot when the energy is 0.
Set to $0A for enemy slots 0 and 1 by enemy_hit_check ($421F) when a blow lands on a leaping enemy (state 8) whose energy is not 0; enemy_leap_hurt ($3B3D) counts it down.

Upper sprite pointers for 20 frames of the walk to the left of an enemy of kind 0 (state 2): $43 five times, $44 five times, $43 five times and $44 five times. enemy_walk_left ($3EA5) reads it at the index $3756,X.
Lower sprite pointers for the same 20 frames: $4A, $4B, $4C and $4D five times each. enemy_walk_left ($3EA5) reads it.
The 20 values of enemy_step for the walk to the left of kind 0, all 0. enemy_walk_left ($3EA5) copies the one at the index to $3752,X.
Upper sprite pointers for 20 frames of the walk to the right of an enemy of kind 0 (state 3): $40 five times, $41 five times, $40 five times and $41 five times. enemy_walk_right ($3DC4) reads it.
Lower sprite pointers for the same 20 frames: $46, $47, $48 and $49 five times each. enemy_walk_right ($3DC4) reads it.
The 20 values of enemy_step for the walk to the right of kind 0, all 0. enemy_walk_right ($3DC4) copies the one at the index to $3752,X.

Upper sprite pointers for 20 frames of the walk to the left of an enemy of any other kind (state 2): $52 five times, $53 five times, $52 five times and $53 five times. enemy_walk_left ($3EA5) reads it.
Lower sprite pointers for the same 20 frames: $4A, $4B, $4C and $4D five times each (the same as walk_a_lower). enemy_walk_left ($3EA5) reads it.
The 20 values of enemy_step for the walk to the left of the other kinds, all 0. enemy_walk_left ($3EA5) reads it.

Upper sprite pointers for 20 frames of the walk to the right of an enemy of any other kind (state 3): $4E five times, $4F five times, $4E five times and $4F five times. enemy_walk_right ($3DC4) reads it.
Lower sprite pointers for the same 20 frames: $46, $47, $48 and $49 five times each (the same as walk_b_lower). enemy_walk_right ($3DC4) reads it.
The 20 values of enemy_step for the walk to the right of the other kinds, all 0. enemy_walk_right ($3DC4) reads it.

The X position of the enemy slot being run, low byte at $384C and high byte at $384D, stored by enemy_frame ($384E). The enemy routines and enemy_hit_check ($421F) put it back when a move would take the enemy to a wall or off the screen.

For enemy slot X: saves the slot's X position in $384C and $384D, takes the address for the state in $3742,X from the table at $38D9 (enemy_state_table), stores it in the operand of the JSR at $386B and calls it.

The operand of the JSR at $386B: enemy_frame ($384E) stores the address of the routine for the slot's state here, low byte at $386C and high byte at $386D, taken from enemy_state_table. The RTS after it at $386E ends enemy_frame.

Sets the point for a tile lookup 8 pixels to the right of enemy slot X and calls tile_at_probe ($309D): X is $3744,X and $3746,X plus 8 plus the fine scroll $1EF3, put in $3063 and $3065, and Y is $3748,X plus $22, put in $3064. A is the screen code under that point. Called by the enemy code at $3E23 and by enemy_hit_check at $42A7.

The same as probe_enemy_right ($386F) for the point 8 pixels to the left of enemy slot X: X is $3744,X and $3746,X minus 8 plus the fine scroll $1EF3. A is the screen code under it. Called by the enemy code at $3F02 and by enemy_hit_check at $4313.

Nine routine addresses, low byte first, one for each enemy state: 0 is enemy_gone ($3CA6), 1 enemy_wait ($3FBA), 2 enemy_walk_left ($3EA5), 3 enemy_walk_right ($3DC4), 4 enemy_throw ($3D4D), 5 enemy_dying ($3CAC), 6 enemy_punch ($3BEC), 7 enemy_punch_left ($3C49) and 8 enemy_leap ($3A15). enemy_frame ($384E) calls the one for the slot's state $3742,X.

Upper sprite pointers for the 99 steps of the leap of an enemy with direction 0 (enemy_leap, $3A15): $65 once, $66 21 times, $67 37 times, $65 10 times, $68 15 times, $60 14 times and $65. The lower pointer is this plus 4.

Upper sprite pointers for the 99 steps of the leap of an enemy with direction 1 (enemy_leap, $3A15): $5D once, $5E 21 times, $5F 37 times, $5D 10 times, $60 15 times, $68 14 times and $5D. The lower pointer is this plus 4.

The height change for each step of the leap (100 bytes): 0, then -4, -3, -2 and -1 for 7 steps each (the enemy rises), 0 twice, then +1, +2, +3 and +4 for 7 steps each (it comes down), $14 40 times (it stays on the ground, with no change of X either), ended by $80. enemy_leap ($3A15) adds the byte at the index $3750,X to the enemy's Y.

Enemy handler for state 8 (a leap), run through enemy_frame ($384E). It clears the step $3752,X, adds 1 to the count $3750,X and reads the height change at that index from leap_dy ($39B1): $14 means no movement; $80 ends the leap, when a random number below $32 makes the enemy turn to face Darkman (enemy_face_player, $4050) and start again at 0, and otherwise holds the last step. Any other change is added to the enemy's Y and the X moves 1 pixel in the direction $374A,X (to the saved X if it would pass $0A on the left). The upper pointer comes from leap_frames_right ($394E) for direction 1 and leap_frames_left ($38EB) for direction 0, the lower is that plus 4. Pointer $60 calls enemy_leap_hit_right ($3B87) and sets the step to 8, pointer $68 calls enemy_leap_hit_left ($3BB9) and sets it to $F8.

The contact test at the end of enemy_leap ($3A15). When Darkman is not stunned ($29F3 is 0), the grace timer hit_grace ($29F4) is 0, the upper pointer is $5F or $67 and enemy_height_test_2 ($3E8A) returns 0, it asks enemy_near_right ($4377) and enemy_near_left ($439B) whether he is within 9 pixels, and if so ORs $1F into his stored stick $203B (no direction), sets the stun timer $29F3 to 4 and hit_grace to $0A and calls player_hurt ($43E4).

The last part of enemy_leap ($3A15), run on every frame. While enemy_hurt $375A,X is 0 it returns. When it is 1 and the energy $3758,X is 0 the enemy is dead: state 0, the exit marker sprite's position $3546-$3548 is set to the enemy's X and Y, and 3 is added to digit 4 of the score through add_digits ($44D1) (300 points by the reckoning of enemy_damage). Otherwise it takes 1 from enemy_hurt and, when the result is even, sets both sprite pointers to $C5 so that the enemy blinks.

Called by enemy_leap ($3A15) for the pointer $60, a blow to the right. When Darkman is not stunned, hit_grace ($29F4) is 0, the heights match (enemy_height_test returns 0) and he is within $1E pixels to the right of the enemy (enemy_left_gap returns 0), it clears the right bit of his stored stick $203B, sets the stun timer $29F3 to 4 and hit_grace to $0A and calls player_hurt ($43E4). A is kept on the stack.
Called by enemy_leap ($3A15) for the pointer $68, a blow to the left. The same as enemy_leap_hit_right ($3B87) with the test enemy_right_gap ($4353) and the left bit of the stick $203B cleared.
The height change of the current step of the leap: enemy_leap ($3A15) sets it to the byte of leap_dy ($39B1), or 0 for $14, and adds it to the enemy's Y.

Enemy handler for state 6 (entry 6 of the table at $38D9), run through enemy_frame ($384E). It adds 1 to the count $3750,X. Below 6 it sets the step $3752,X to 0 and the wind-up frame ($3F46). From 6 to $13 it sets the attack frame and step ($3F76) and, when the enemy is level with Darkman ($3E67 returns 0) and he is within $1E pixels to its right ($432F returns 0), at count 6 it clears bit 3 of the joystick byte $203B, sets the stun timer $29F3 to 4 and calls player_hurt ($43E4). From $14 to $1D it shows the wind-up frame again; at $1E it sets the step to 0, the state $3742,X to 1 and the count to a random number divided by 8.

Enemy handler for state 7 (a punch to the left), run through enemy_frame ($384E), the mirror of enemy_punch ($3BEC). It adds 1 to the count $3750,X. Below 6 it shows the wind-up frame; from 6 to $13 the attack frame, and at count 6, when the enemy is level with Darkman and within $1E pixels to his right (enemy_right_gap returns 0), it clears the left bit of his stick $203B, sets the stun timer $29F3 to 4 and calls player_hurt ($43E4). From $14 to $1D it shows the wind-up frame again and at $1E it returns to state 1 with a random count.
Enemy handler for state 0, run through enemy_frame ($384E): sets the enemy's Y $3748,X to 0, which puts its sprites at the top of the screen.

Enemy handler for state 5 (dying), run through enemy_frame ($384E). Clears the step and adds 1 to the count $3750,X. The upper and lower pointers go through a falling sequence: $56 and $57 (kind 0) or $5A and $57 (other kinds) below count $0F, then $C5 with $58 or $5B below $1E, then $C5 with $59 or $5C up to $59. At count $5A it plays sound effect 9 (X = $24) through $B0EE; after that the enemy blinks, with both pointers $C5 on every second frame, until count $A0, when the state goes to 0.
The blink toggle of enemy slot 0 ($3D4B) and slot 1 ($3D4C): enemy_dying ($3CAC) flips it on every frame after count $5A, and shows the blank pointer $C5 while it is 0.

Enemy handler for state 4 (throwing), run through enemy_frame ($384E). Adds 1 to the count $3750,X. It shows a wind-up pose (upper $50 and lower $46 for direction 1, $54 and $4A for direction 0) below count 10 and again from count $2F to $31, and a throwing pose with the upper sprite shifted 8 pixels (upper $51 or $55) from count 10 to $29 and from $2B to $2E. At count $2A it calls enemy_shoot ($40C1); from $32 on it returns to state 1 with a random count.

Enemy handler for state 3 (walking right), run through enemy_frame ($384E). Sets the step to 0 and the direction to 1. When the enemy is level with Darkman (enemy_height_test) and he is within $1E pixels to its right (enemy_left_gap) it switches to state 6, the punch, with count 0. Otherwise a zero count calls enemy_decide ($3FD2); else it counts down, moves 2 pixels right (back to the saved X, and enemy_decide, past X $13C or when the tile ahead is $30) and takes the pointers and step from walk_b ($3798) for kind 0 and walk_d ($3810) for the others, at the index $3756,X.

Returns A=0 when enemy slot X is level with Darkman and A=1 when it is not: the enemy's height $3748,X is compared with his $2658, and the answer is 0 when they are equal, when the enemy is less than $1C lines below him and when it is less than $0A lines above him. Called by the enemy code at $3B92, $3BC4, $3C09, $3C66, $3DCE and $3EAD.

Returns A=0 when enemy slot X is level with Darkman or above him by up to $1D lines, and A=1 otherwise: the enemy's height $3748,X is compared with his $2658, the answer is 0 when they are equal or when the enemy is above him by less than $1E lines, and 1 when it is below him. Called by enemy_leap_contact ($3AFE) at $3B13.

Enemy handler for state 2 (walking left), run through enemy_frame ($384E). Sets the step and the direction to 0. When the enemy is level with Darkman (enemy_height_test) and within $1E pixels to his right (enemy_right_gap returns 0) it switches to state 7, the punch to the left, with count 0. Otherwise a zero count calls enemy_decide ($3FD2); else it counts down, moves 2 pixels left (back to the saved X, and enemy_decide, below X $1E or when the tile ahead is $35) and takes the pointers and step from walk_a ($375C) for kind 0 and walk_c ($37D4) for the others, at the index $3756,X.

Sets the sprite pointers of enemy slot X for its wind-up pose, the upper in $374C,X and the lower in $374E,X. For a kind $3754,X of 0 the pair is $43 and $4A when the direction $374A,X is 0 and $40 and $46 otherwise; for any other kind $52 and $4A when the direction is 0 and $4E and $46 otherwise. Called by enemy_punch ($3BEC) at $3BFE, by enemy_punch_left at $3C5B and by enemy_wait at $3FBF.

Sets the step $3752,X to $F8 (direction $374A,X 0) or $08 and the sprite pointers of enemy slot X for its attack pose, the upper in $374C,X and the lower in $374E,X. For a kind $3754,X of 0 the pair is $45 and $4A (direction 0) or $42 and $46; for any other kind $6E and $4A (direction 0) or $6D and $46. Called by enemy_punch ($3BEC) at $3C06 and by enemy_punch_left at $3C63.
Enemy handler for state 1 (waiting), run through enemy_frame ($384E). Clears the step, shows the wind-up pose and counts the count $3750,X down; when it is 0 it calls enemy_decide ($3FD2).

Chooses the next state of enemy slot X. At the left edge (X below $1E) it walks right (state 3) and at the right edge (X from $128) left (state 2), each with a random count of 0 to 31. Otherwise a random number picks: below $40 wait (state 1, count 0 to 15); $E6 or more, throw (state 4, after facing Darkman) when no shot is on the screen and the kind is not 0, otherwise wait; in between, a walk toward Darkman or in a random direction. Called by the enemy routines when a count runs out, and by the walks when a move meets a wall or the edge ($3E1F, $3EFE).

Sets the direction $374A,X of enemy slot X to face Darkman: 1 when his X ($2657/$2659) is greater than the enemy's, 0 when it is less, unchanged when they are equal. Called by enemy_leap ($3A15), enemy_decide ($3FD2) at $4012 and $4042.
While it is not zero scroll_step ($2066) does nothing. exit_marker_step ($354A) sets it to 1 when an enemy is in play and clears it when none is and the end flag $2061 is clear; play_setup clears it.

Compares the 16-bit value that the pointer $85/$86 points at with the scroll position scroll_pos ($1A1F/$1A20): when its high byte equals $1A20 and its low byte is below $1A1F it sets scroll_stop ($4079) to 1. Nothing calls it or jumps to it; play_setup ($1AB5) and exit_marker_step ($354A) are the only other code that sets $4079, and scroll_step ($2066) reads it.
Set to 1 while a shot is on the screen; shot_draw ($4140) moves it, shot_erase ($41EF) takes it off and shot_touch_test ($4636) clears it on a hit.

Tests whether Darkman's blow hits enemy slot X; move_enemies ($3725) runs it for both slots. Returns A=0 when Darkman is up to 9 pixels to the right of enemy slot X (his X $2657/$2659 minus the enemy's $3744,X/$3746,X is from 0 to 9), otherwise A=1. Called by enemy_leap_contact ($3AFE) at $3B1A.
Returns A=0 when Darkman is up to 9 pixels to the left of enemy slot X (the enemy's X minus his X is from 0 to 9), otherwise A=1. Called by enemy_leap_contact ($3AFE) at $3B21.

A copy of Darkman's energy ($43E3) that draw_bar ($4449) counts up to $21 while it cuts the bar.

Countdown of scan_wait ($4B83) between two colour swaps, reloaded with $D2.

Erodes the buffer $FE00-$FEFF in 30 rounds. The operand of the AND at $4CB8: dissolve_pattern ($4C8E) stores the mask it chose for each byte here before the AND runs.

Exchanges 256 bytes of $C800 with $C000, $68 bytes of $C900 with $C100, 256 bytes of $C968 with $C600 and 256 bytes of $CA68 with $C700. Called by mask_finish at $4C2E and $4C52.

Called by mask_finish at $4C31.

Set to $11 by fire_capture ($4EC7) on a capture and to 0 by mask_setup ($58C8). No code reads it. The byte after it, $4EC5, is not used.

Returns X=0 to 4 from a random byte ($1FB5): 0 below $32, 1 below $64, 2 below $96, 3 below $C8, else 4. Called by objects_spawn ($533E).

Low byte of the source address that object_flip ($53D9) reads the picture from ($E7 or $17 after the toggle, or $FF).

Sprite shapes for pointers $97 to $9C (384 bytes): the player walking right (walk_right_frames at $26E8). The same bytes as level 2's walk_right_shapes.

Sprite shapes for pointers $9D to $A2 (384 bytes): the player walking left (walk_left_frames at $26D6), drawn like walk_right_shapes, with $AA to $AF and $86 to $8B as the other two sprites. The same bytes as level 2's walk_left_shapes.
Sprite shapes for pointers $A3 to $B2 (1,024 bytes). The same bytes as level 2's attack_shapes.

Sprite shapes for pointers $B3 to $C1 (960 bytes), the rest of attack_shapes: punch_frames ($2D91) uses $B4, $B5, $BE and $BF, crouch_frames ($2743) $B6, $B7, $C0 and $C1 and strike_frames ($2E30) $BB, and $B8 to $BA are the second sprite of the player climbing (F + $24, see climb_shapes). The same bytes as level 2's attack_shapes_b.

Sprite shapes for pointers $C2 to $C5 (256 bytes): $C2 to $C4 the third sprite of the player climbing (F + $2E, see climb_shapes), the same bytes as level 2's shapes_unreferenced; $C5 ($F140) is 64 zero bytes, the blank sprite that enemy_dying ($3CAC) and marker_frames ($3518) use.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $C6 to $CD (512 bytes), then 1,088 zero bytes to $F7BF (pointers $CE to $DE): the objects of objects_step ($3297). object_wide_frames ($3466) uses $C6, $C8 and $CA, and object_wide gives the second sprite the pointer plus 1 ($C7, $C9 and $CB); object_small_frames ($33F8) uses $CC and $CD. Pointer $C5 ($F140) is the blank sprite, 64 zero bytes at the end of the block at $F080.

The status panel's bitmap, which the raster interrupt irq_bottom switches on from line $CD (bitmap mode at $E000, multicolour): 40 cells wide, rows 19 to 24, 8 bytes a cell and 320 a row. The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap.

Row 0 of the pixel rows of pictures A and B: row 19, columns 32 to 37 of the panel bitmap (48 bytes). image_a_draw ($4765), image_b_draw ($47CE) and image_flash ($470C) write the first of their five 48-byte rows here; the other four are image_row_1 ($FA00), image_row_2 ($FB40), image_row_3 ($FC80) and image_row_4 ($FDC0).
Row 19, columns 38 and 39, and row 20, columns 0 to 26: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (232 bytes). The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_1.
Row 20, columns 27 to 31 (40 bytes): timer_draw ($5C29) draws the three timer digits into the cells at $F9D8, $F9E8 and $F9F0.
Row 1 of the pixel rows of pictures A and B (see $F8C0). The same bytes as level 2's panel_picture_1.
Row 20, columns 38 and 39, and row 21, columns 0 to 2: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (40 bytes). The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_2.
Row 21, columns 3 to 9 of the panel bitmap (56 bytes): draw_figures ($44FD) draws the seven score digits from $0A00 into these cells, 8 bytes each, from digit_glyphs ($4536).
Row 21, columns 10 to 16: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (56 bytes). The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_3.
Row 21, columns 17 to 24 of the panel bitmap (64 bytes): the eight cells of the energy bar, which draw_bar ($4449) writes.
Row 21, columns 25 to 31: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (56 bytes). The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_4.
Row 2 of the pixel rows of pictures A and B: row 21, columns 32 to 37 of the panel bitmap (48 bytes); see image_row_0 ($F8C0).
Row 21, columns 38 and 39, and row 22, columns 0 to 31: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (272 bytes). The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_5.
Row 3 of the pixel rows of pictures A and B: row 22, columns 32 to 37 of the panel bitmap (48 bytes); see image_row_0 ($F8C0).
Row 22, columns 38 and 39, and row 23, columns 0 to 31: panel bitmap that no traced routine writes (272 bytes). The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_6.
Row 4 of the pixel rows of pictures A and B (see $F8C0). The same bytes as level 2's panel_picture_4.

Row 23, columns 38 and 39, and all of row 24 (336 bytes). load_panel_bitmap ($1C36) copies $FE00-$FEFF from $1C42 when play starts; in the mask game mask_setup ($58C8) fills those 256 bytes with $AA and dissolve_pattern ($4C8E) erodes and clears them, as the shapes of sprites 1 to 4 (pointers $F8 to $FB). The rest is panel bitmap that no traced routine writes. The same bytes as level 2's panel_bitmap_7.

Shape address = $C000 + 64 x pointer. Sprite shapes for pointers $FD ($FF40) and $FE ($FF80), 128 bytes: $FE is the first frame of the exit marker, the pointer that marker_frames ($3518) holds for 24 steps. No table found sets $FD.
